evidence: audit-scratch/ontology-report-card.md; run-agent:7806 (validator soft/user-only); 20260610_adam_backend.sql:39-41 (RLS for-all owner_id=auth.uid()); executed: direct supabase.update() set gateReviews.frame.status='approved' on 5f0a108b… → writeError:null, persisted, self-approved; restored to {}
expected: A gate approval must be mediated server-side: readiness checked, approver role verified, approver != author, and an approved artifact made immutable.
actual: gateReviews lives in the owner-writable JSONB blob. A direct API update (bypassing the UI, onRecordGate, and all artifact-readiness checks) set an 'approved' gate and self-approved with no server rejection. The only guard is RLS ownership; there is no author!=approver separation and no server-side immutability of an approved artifact.
impact: Any authenticated owner can mark any gate approved and edit approved artifacts by direct API call. Governance is convention, not enforcement. Per the audit S1 definition ('a governance gate can be bypassed'), this is existential for the 'governed software' claim. Bounded today by the single-owner-per-programme trust model (the owner is the sole actor), which is the only reason it is not immediately catastrophic.
recommendation: Move gate approval behind an edge function (SECURITY DEFINER) that (a) verifies artifact readiness server-side, (b) checks the caller's role, (c) enforces approver!=author, (d) writes an append-only, immutable approval record; make the client update path unable to set gateReviews.*.status directly (RLS column/JSONB policy or move gateReviews out of the client-writable blob).
